subject_group: 6.1.10 Vertical/short takeoff and landing air vehicles

versions.text: Criterion: Verify that vertical takeoff (VTO) is safe. Standard: The air vehicle meets the standards within MIL-STD-1797, 5.2.7.1.2 Vertical takeoff (VTO). Method of Compliance: Verification methods include analysis, test, demonstration, simulation, and inspection of process, design, test, or configuration documentation.

Standard: The air vehicle is no worse than Level 2 flying qualities for all VTOs, land and shipboard. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Analysis.
(1) Conduct analysis of all VTOs to evaluate air vehicle capabilities and control margins during VTOs, to include: a. Land-based hover pit VTO. b. Land-based hover pad VTO. c. Shipboard VTO. d. Rolling VTO. e. Creeping VTO. f. Baseline control system. g. Precision hover modes. Test.
  (1) Lab test: Conduct piloted simulation and evaluation to assess flying/handling qualities as specified in MIL-STD-1797, Vertical Takeoff (VTO) paragraph for each combination of air vehicle states, control modes, and environmental conditions, to include: a. Land-based hover pit VTO. b. Land-based hover pad VTO. c. Shipboard VTO. d. Rolling VTO. e. Creeping VTO. f. Baseline control system. g. Precision hover modes. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
  (2) Flight test: Conduct flight test to assess flying/handling qualities as specified in MIL-STD- 1797, Vertical Takeoff (VTO) paragraph for selected combinations of air vehicle states, control modes, and environmental conditions, to include: a. Land-based hover pit VTO. b. Land-based hover pad VTO. c. Shipboard VTO. d. Rolling VTO. e. Creeping VTO. f. Baseline control system. g. Precision hover modes.
